item.title: Incarico post-doc: A framework for low-resolution data acquisition (Univ. PERUGIA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-11 23:59
Institution: Univ. PERUGIA, Perugia
Field: Industrial and information engineering / 09/IMIS-01 Misure

This project aims at developing a framework enabling measurements based on quantified signals using few bits or even one-bit. It will address the problem of estimating the parameters of signals, such as amplitude, frequency, time-of-arrival, delays, noise magnitudes, based on their binary version or of a very low-resolution, coarse representation. The central question in this project is how we process low-resolution / one-bit data to provide enough information on the full-resolution signal, after severe quantization.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: 2026-IpdDip-03-diii - Research of Ultra-Wideband Noise-Cancelling CMOS LNA Solutions for FEM-Less Receivers (Univ. PAVIA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-25 12:00
Institution: Univ. PAVIA, Pavia
Field: Industrial and information engineering / 09/IINF-01 Elettronica

State-of-the art receiver architectures rely on multiple cascaded GaAs LNA stages integrated within the front-end module (FEM), followed by a PCB balun that interfaces the FEM with the CMOS integrated circuit. This approach provides high performance, but increases power consumption, cost, and overall system complexity. The scope of this project is to find a CMOS-based wideband LNA architecture that can overcome these challenges by exploiting advanced noise cancellation and analog linearization techniques. The goal is to approach the RF performance of GaAs-based LNAs with equal or lower power dissipation. The research will include architecture development, circuit design, layout, and silicon…

item.title: Incarico post-doc: CFD analysis of an air system for thermal storage with PCM (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-04 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Industrial and information engineering / 09/ICHI-01 Sistemi, metodi e tecnologie dell'ingegneria chimica e di processo

The research project focuses on the fluid-dynamic and thermal study and optimization of a Thermal Energy Storage (TES) system based on Phase Change Materials (PCM), using air as the heat transfer fluid. The objective is to develop and validate transient Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulation models to analyze the charging (melting) and discharging (solidification) processes of the PCM. The study will evaluate different heat exchanger geometries and operating air parameters to overcome the low thermal conductivity limitation of PCMs, thereby maximizing heat transfer efficiency.
